name: Bench press
angleNote: Bar height: 0% = on the chest, 100% = arms locked out. Torques are per arm; drag the figure to turn it.
momentArmNote: Moment arm = the joint's 3D distance from the bar's push line through that hand; it feeds every component of that joint's torque.

muscles.name: Pectoralis major
muscles.note: Main horizontal adductor: brings the upper arms in across the chest. Wider grips load it more.

muscles.name: Anterior deltoid
muscles.note: Shoulder flexor; also helps horizontal adduction.

muscles.name: Triceps
muscles.note: Elbow extensor. Its torque depends on where the hands sit relative to the elbows, which only shows up in 3D.

muscles.name: Infraspinatus, teres minor
muscles.note: External rotators of the rotator cuff: hold the upper arm from turning inwards.

muscles.name: Subscapularis
muscles.note: Internal rotator of the rotator cuff: holds the upper arm from turning outwards.

phases.name: Off the chest
phases.text: Bar on the chest, furthest in front of the shoulder: the shoulder's largest moment arm.

phases.name: Mid-range
phases.text: The bar moves back over the shoulder as it rises.

phases.name: Lockout
phases.text: Bar over the shoulders: little shoulder torque; whatever the elbows still do depends on the grip.

variants.name: Flat bench, medium grip
variants.notes: Hands about 1.7× shoulder width, elbows stacked under the hands in the front view. The flare angle follows from the arm's geometry (shown under the table). Each hand pushes straight up with half the bar (it isn't pulled apart or squeezed), and the shoulder joints stay put; real shoulder blades move, so the mid-press elbow numbers are probably on the high side.

variants.name: Wide grip
variants.notes: Hands far out: the upper arms flare, the pecs (horizontal adduction) work much harder and the triceps much less. The bar also travels less. Each hand pushes straight up with half the bar (it isn't pulled apart or squeezed), and the shoulder joints stay put; real shoulder blades move, so the mid-press elbow numbers are probably on the high side.

variants.name: Close grip
variants.notes: Hands at shoulder width, elbows tucked: the triceps take over and the pecs' across-the-body work nearly vanishes. Each hand pushes straight up with half the bar (it isn't pulled apart or squeezed), and the shoulder joints stay put; real shoulder blades move, so the mid-press elbow numbers are probably on the high side.

variants.name: Medium grip, elbows flared past the hands
variants.notes: Elbows pushed 6 cm outside the hands and the bar lowered higher on the chest: see how the rotation torque and flare angle change. Each hand pushes straight up with half the bar (it isn't pulled apart or squeezed), and the shoulder joints stay put; real shoulder blades move, so the mid-press elbow numbers are probably on the high side.

variants.name: Incline bench (30°), medium grip
variants.notes: Bench tilted 30°: the bar touches the upper chest and presses vertically over the shoulders. Each hand pushes straight up with half the bar (it isn't pulled apart or squeezed), and the shoulder joints stay put; real shoulder blades move, so the mid-press elbow numbers are probably on the high side.
